documents.title: Generative AI (teaching guide)
tiers: Sample course statements from complete exclusion of AI to AI fully embedded
documents.summary: Teaching-center guide for faculty that leaves AI decisions to instructors and urges them to state boundaries early. It favors AI literacy over policing, names Copilot and Adobe Express as approved tools, and points to sample course statements.
documents.stance_why: The guide says "you will determine how generative AI and other technology will be used or limited in your courses" and points to sample statements "ranging from complete exclusion of all AI use in a course to embedding AI fully", so it sets no rule and hands the decision to instructors.

units.why: Guidance says "you will determine how generative AI and other technology will be used or limited in your courses", so the decision sits with instructors: P04, not a tier list; informs because it states who decides.
units.anchor: you will determine how generative AI and other technology will be used or limited in
units.policy: As educators and instructors, you will determine how generative AI and other technology will be used or limited in your courses.

units.why: The teaching guide says it is "essential that you communicate early and often with your learners about the boundaries of generative AI"; that asks instructors to state AI expectations (P09), addressed to instructors, at course start.
units.anchor: communicate early and often with your learners about the boundaries of generative AI

units.why: "policing AI use is nearing impossible" concedes limits on control, which is P82 (cannot be fully prevented); it is a factual claim, so informs.
units.anchor: policing AI use is nearing impossible

units.anchor: AI Literacy offers a strong alternative to policing and detection approaches.
units.fit_note: Also recommends AI literacy as the replacement for policing, which P60 does not mention.

units.why: "Generative AI is being used heavily in industry and disciplines. It will be essential that our students develop an AI Literacy" gives the career reason for teaching AI use: P44.

units.policy: It will be essential that our students develop an AI Literacy and become responsible users of AI platforms. Therefore, avoiding discussion about AI in our courses is likely not helpful and policing AI use is nearing impossible.

units.why: "Preparing your students through AI Literacy ... will become an essential skill" frames AI literacy (evaluating, navigating, ethically using) as a skill to teach: P44.
units.anchor: will become an essential skill

documents.title: Academic Integrity Policy (incl. Appendix C: Academic Integrity for Generative AI)
documents.summary: Appendix C extends the undergraduate Academic Integrity Policy to generative AI. Instructors decide whether AI is allowed and must state it, students must follow and cite as directed and own their work, and silent syllabi are treated as help from another person. It supplies sample statements from ban to requirement. Only the Appendix C text and its linked rules were coded, not the general integrity procedures.

units.why: Appendix C says the guidelines "serve as an extension to the existing Academic Integrity Policy" and cover all undergraduates; this is scope-setting (P56) rather than a rule.
units.anchor: are applicable to all members of the undergraduate student body.

units.why: "the basic rules of academic integrity apply: all violations of this policy are in some way acts of dishonesty" classes misuse as academic dishonesty: P36.
units.anchor: the basic rules of academic integrity apply: all violations of this policy are in some
units.policy: Fundamentally, however, the basic rules of academic integrity apply: all violations of this policy are in some way acts of dishonesty in that they use unauthorized or falsified materials, processes, or resources.

documents.title: For Students
documents.summary: Student resource page from the AI Oversight Committee. It warns about privacy, cost, bias and hallucination, tells students to use UNCG tools, talk to their professor, check and acknowledge AI output, and keep their own critical thinking. It sets no AI-use rule of its own.
documents.stance_why: The page tells students to "Talk to your professor about how and where GenAI-based tools can be used in your course" and "consult with your professor/instructor", setting no stance of its own and deferring to the course instructor.

units.why: "Do not share information that is considered private, or sensitive, such as credit card information, personal details such as ID numbers or addresses" protects personal data: P50.
units.anchor: Do not share information that is considered private, or sensitive, such as credit card information

units.why: "Be wary of tools that require a credit card to sign up for it to start a free trial" warns about subscription traps; no type covers consumer-cost caution (P51 is about equity of access).
units.anchor: Be wary of tools that require a credit card to sign up for it to
units.policy: Be wary of tools that require a credit card to sign up for it to start a free trial, as they may employ tactics that make it harder to then cancel the subscription.
units.uncovered_note: Caution about misleading free-trial costs and hard-to-cancel subscriptions when choosing an AI tool.

units.why: "ensure that they are legitimate resources" asks students to vet tools outside UNCG's offerings: P50 (prefer vetted tools).
units.anchor: ensure that they are legitimate resources.

units.why: "GenAI is not sentient" and models are "simply systems trained on large and biased datasets"; stresses AI is not a person. P96 is nearest but concerns authorship and sources.
units.anchor: GenAI models or Large Language models (LLMs) might appear to possess sentience or self-awareness as
units.policy: GenAI models or Large Language models (LLMs) might appear to possess sentience or self-awareness as a human would, but are simply systems trained on large and biased datasets. LLMs are designed to output the most likely, or most common results possible based on their data, and will invariably tend to suppress less common or marginalized information.
units.fit_note: Says AI only appears sentient; does not address authorship or citation.

units.why: "will invariably tend to suppress less common or marginalized information" names a bias harm: P53.
units.anchor: will invariably tend to suppress less common or marginalized information.

units.why: "GenAI models carry implicit biases ... and should not be used in those circumstances" (ethical deliberation and decision); names bias and discourages that use: P53.
units.anchor: unsuitable for use in cases of ethical deliberation and decision and should not be used
units.policy: GenAI models carry implicit biases in them that make them unsuitable for use in cases of ethical deliberation and decision and should not be used in those circumstances. Furthermore, this data is from the past, which results in a loss of context for current social changes.

units.why: "GenAI in its current stage will tend to 'hallucinate' or make up random data that is not true" is the accuracy warning: P31.
units.anchor: GenAI in its current stage will tend to ‘hallucinate’ or make up random data that
units.policy: GenAI in its current stage will tend to ‘hallucinate’ or make up random data that is not true. Models have no real sense of what is true or false.

units.why: "Use UNCG's offerings that ensure your data privacy and security" tells students to use university tools: P92.
units.anchor: Use UNCG’s offerings that ensure your data privacy and security.

units.why: "Talk to your professor about how and where GenAI-based tools can be used in your course" is asking the instructor: P10.
units.anchor: Talk to your professor about how and where GenAI-based tools can be used in your
units.policy: Talk to your professor about how and where GenAI-based tools can be used in your course. Seek clarity on issues of syllabus wording, citation, and methods of use.

units.why: "Do not cite information from GenAI as the truth ... Always check the citations that it provides" requires verification: P31.
units.anchor: Do not cite information from GenAI as the truth for the information it presents.

units.why: "You can also reach out to the Librarian for assistance in your research" points to human help: P72.
units.anchor: You can also reach out to the Librarian for assistance in your research.
